propositions.text: The claimant, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of India.
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of India.

propositions.text: The claim is based on section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.
propositions.quote: He is basing his claim on section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal states the claimant is an Indian citizen claiming under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: A friend of the claimant's brother named XXXX had problems with the police in 2011.
propositions.quote: A friend of the claimant's brother named XXXX had problems with the police in 2011.

propositions.text: Police suspected XXXX of terrorist ties and turned to the claimant's brother when XXXX left the country.
propositions.quote: They suspected him of having ties to terrorists, and they turned to the claimant's brother when XXXX left the country.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal recounts that the claimant's brother's friend had police trouble in 2011, leading police to target the brother.

propositions.text: The claimant's brother left India for the US in 2011 due to police pressure, which then shifted to the claimant's family.
propositions.quote: The claimant's brother left India for the United States in XXXX 2011 because he could no longer bear the pressure from police, who then turned against the other members of the claimant's family.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal states the claimant's brother left India for the US in 2011 due to police pressure, which then shifted to the family.

propositions.text: The claimant came to Canada in 2011 for an event, then returned to India.
propositions.quote: The claimant came to Canada in XXXX 2011 to take part in XXXX XXXX XXXX. Afterwards, he returned to India.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal notes the claimant visited Canada in 2011 for an event and then returned to India.

propositions.text: In 2011, the claimant was arrested and detained for several days by police accusing him of militant ties.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2011, the claimant was arrested and detained for XXXX days by police officers who accused him having ties with militants abroad.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal states the claimant was arrested and detained in 2011 by police accusing him of militant ties.

propositions.text: The claimant went to Delhi to wait to leave India, arrived in Canada in 2012, and claimed refugee protection two weeks later.
propositions.quote: He arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2012, and claimed refugee protection around two weeks later.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal states the claimant waited in Delhi, then came to Canada in 2012 and claimed refugee protection two weeks later.

propositions.text: The claimant fears returning to India over three years after leaving, believing police still want to pursue him.
propositions.quote: He fears returning to India, over three years after he left, because he believes the police still want to go after him.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal states the claimant fears returning to India, believing police still seek him.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claimant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 or 97(1).
propositions.quote: the panel determines that he is not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity based on documents, including his passport.
propositions.quote: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity based on the documents filed on the record, including a copy of his passport.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal is satisfied with the claimant's identity based on documentary evidence.

propositions.text: The claimant testified at the hearing.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified at the hearing.

propositions.text: The panel noted several points undermining the claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: The panel noted a number of points that undermine his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal notes the claimant testified and identifies several credibility concerns.

propositions.text: The claimant stated that XXXX, a Muslim friend of his brother, had police problems starting in 2011.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that XXXX, a Muslim friend of his older brother XXXX, had problems with the police starting in 2011.

propositions.text: They all lived in the same village, which the claimant says has a large population.
propositions.quote: They all lived in the same village, which, according to the claimant, has around XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX residents.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal recounts the claimant's statement about his brother's friend having police trouble in 2011 and their large village.

propositions.text: The police accused XXXX of terrorist ties and, after he left, harassed and arrested the claimant's brother to get information.
propositions.quote: the police accused XXXX of having ties to terrorists and that after he left the village, the police turned to XXXX, whom they harassed and arrested a number of times so that he would provide information on XXXX and the supposed plans of the militants.

propositions.text: On at least three occasions, the claimant's father allegedly paid bribes for his son XXXX's release.
propositions.quote: On at least three occasions, the claimant's father allegedly had to pay bribes for his son XXXX to be released.

propositions.text: The pressure led XXXX to leave India for the US in 2010.
propositions.quote: Apparently, the pressure was such that XXXX left India for the United States in XXXX 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges police accused XXXX of terrorist ties, harassed his brother, required bribes, and forced his brother to leave for the US.

propositions.text: After XXXX left, police allegedly targeted the claimant's family with operations, searches, and mistreatment, seeking information on terrorists.
propositions.quote: the police allegedly came after the claimant's family. The claimant described operations that took place at his house during which the police arrived in three or four vehicles, surrounded the house, asked questions, searched, and mistreated his family.

propositions.text: Each time, his father had to pay bribes for police to leave.
propositions.quote: Each time, his father had to pay bribes for them to leave.

propositions.text: The claimant was present for at least two operations and was questioned about XXXX, his brother, and terrorists' plans.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he was present for at least two of these operations. He was asked questions about XXXX, XXXX and the terrorists' plans.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges police targeted his family, conducted operations, required bribes, and questioned him about terrorists' plans.

propositions.text: The claimant came to Canada in 2011 for an event, stayed three days, did not claim refugee protection, and returned to India.
propositions.quote: the claimant came to Canada in XXXX 2011 to participate in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX He stayed in the country for about three days without claiming refugee protection. He claimed that he then returned to India because he had no intention of staying in Canada.

propositions.text: The claimant acknowledged his brother had sought refuge in the US but said he had no direct problems then.
propositions.quote: He acknowledged that his brother had sought refuge in the United States then but submitted that he had no direct problems.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal notes the claimant visited Canada in 2011, did not claim protection, and returned to India, stating he had no direct problems then.

propositions.text: The claimant stated he was arrested and detained by police for several days in 2011.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he was arrested and detained by police for XXXX days in XXXX 2011.

propositions.text: When asked about other arrests, the claimant hesitated, then admitted to other arrests not mentioned in his PIF due to 'oversight.'
propositions.quote: He finally answered that he had been arrested and taken to the station on other occasions. He explained that these two arrests are not in his narrative attached to his Personal Information Form (PIF) because of an oversight.

propositions.text: He claimed he forgot to mention the other arrests because he was focused on his main arrest.
propositions.quote: He supposedly [translation] "forgot" to write them down because he had been focusing on his arrest.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal notes the claimant described a 2011 arrest, hesitated about others, then admitted to more arrests omitted from his PIF due to 'oversight.'

propositions.text: The claimant stated he stayed in Delhi for six months waiting for documents to leave for Canada and had no problems there.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he stayed in Delhi for six (6) months waiting to obtain the documents that would allow him to return to Canada. He supposedly did not have any problems during his stay.

propositions.text: He stated he had no problems in Delhi because he was in hiding.
propositions.quote: He stated that this is because he was in hiding.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal notes the claimant stayed in Delhi for six months without problems, claiming he was in hiding.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant's failure to claim protection in Canada in 2011 inconsistent with someone fearing for his life.
propositions.quote: the panel considers the fact that the claimant did not claim refugee protection when he travelled to Canada in XXXX 2011 to be behaviour that is inconsistent with that of someone who fears for his life.

propositions.text: It finds it implausible the claimant returned home because he did not feel targeted, given his statements about police harassment.
propositions.quote: It finds it implausible, in the particular circumstances of this case, that the claimant made the decision to return home because he did not feel targeted, even though, according to his statements, the police had harassed his brother to the point that he left India for the United States and had carried out several large-scale operations at his home.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds the claimant's actions inconsistent with fear for his life and implausible given his statements about police harassment.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the omission of two arrests from the PIF was an oversight, but an attempt to embellish his story.
propositions.quote: the panel considers this an attempt to embellish his story during the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds the claimant's omission of two arrests from his PIF was not an oversight but an attempt to embellish his story.

propositions.text: The panel considers the claimant's trouble-free six-month stay in Delhi as evidence police are not interested in him outside his village.
propositions.quote: the panel considers the fact that the claimant stayed in Delhi for six months without experiencing any problems to be an indication that the police are not interested in him outside his village.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds the claimant's uneventful stay in Delhi suggests police are not interested in him outside his village.

propositions.text: The panel draws a negative inference from these points, affecting its analysis of an internal flight alternative in Delhi.
propositions.quote: The panel draws a negative inference from these points. This inference affects its analysis of whether there is an internal flight alternative in Delhi.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal draws a negative inference from the claimant's actions, impacting its analysis of an internal flight alternative in Delhi.

propositions.text: The test for a flight alternative is two-pronged: safe location and reasonableness of relocation.
propositions.quote: The test for a flight alternative is two-pronged. First, the panel must examine whether there is a location where the claimant could safely relocate. Second, it must determine whether it is unreasonable to expect the claimant to relocate to that safe location.

paragraphs.summary: The panel states the two-part legal test for a flight alternative: safety and reasonableness of relocation.

propositions.text: The panel asked the claimant what would happen if he returned to Delhi or Mumbai after three years.
propositions.quote: When asked what would happen to him if he returned to live in Delhi or Mumbai, three years after having left, the claimant responded...

propositions.text: The claimant says registering to work and live in Delhi or Mumbai would expose his information to police and put him in danger again.
propositions.quote: he would have to register to work and live in those locations, which would mean that his personal information could be communicated to the police and he could be put in danger again.

paragraphs.summary: The panel asked the claimant about returning to Delhi or Mumbai; the claimant argued registration would expose him to police danger.

propositions.text: The panel disagrees with the claimant's argument about danger from registering in Delhi or Mumbai.
propositions.quote: The panel does not agree.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's argument about the danger of registering in Delhi or Mumbai.

propositions.text: The claimant's story shows local police were interested in his brother, family, and him, and bribes were paid multiple times.
propositions.quote: The claimant's story indicates that it was the local police who were interested in his brother, and then in his family and in him, and that bribes were paid to them on multiple occasions.

propositions.text: The panel asked the claimant to explain why police left after bribes were paid.
propositions.quote: When the panel wanted him to explain how the police had paid visits to his family on multiple occasions and then left them alone after a bribe was paid, the claimant answered...

propositions.text: The claimant explained that in India, police harass people for bribes as a business.
propositions.quote: that is how things work in India, they harass people to get money, it is a business.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes the claimant's story involves local police seeking bribes, and the claimant says police harassment is for money in India.

propositions.text: The claimant has not shown Delhi is unsafe for relocation.
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the claimant has failed to discharge his burden of demonstrating that Delhi is not a safe location where he could relocate.

propositions.text: It is unlikely local authorities from his village would pursue him in Delhi after three years, given their prior interest was for bribes.
propositions.quote: It does not see how, three years after leaving, the claimant could be of sufficient interest to the local authorities in his village-which is in a different state-for them to deploy the necessary resources to search for him, whereas they had actually profited from the situation to squeeze bribes from the family.

propositions.text: The claim that registering in Delhi would alert corrupt village authorities is speculative; no evidence his information is flagged.
propositions.quote: it considers the claimant's allegations that his registering in Delhi would result in the corrupt authorities of his village being able to locate him to be speculation, since nothing indicates that his personal information is flagged and would necessarily come to their attention.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant failed to show Delhi is unsafe, doubts village police would pursue him, and calls his registration fears speculative.

propositions.text: The claimant's family still lives in Haryana three years later.
propositions.quote: the panel notes that the claimant stated that his family still lives in the state of Haryana, three years later.

propositions.text: The claimant says his family moved within Haryana due to ongoing harassment by local authorities.
propositions.quote: The claimant submits that they had to move to a different community because they were still being harassed by the local authorities.

propositions.text: The panel asked how the family could live in Haryana without problems.
propositions.quote: However, when the panel asked him to explain how they were still living in the same state without experiencing any problems, the claimant responded...

propositions.text: The claimant responded his father pays expenses and Haryana is large.
propositions.quote: his father has XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to pay for expenses and that Haryana is a large state.

propositions.text: The panel sees this as showing the claimant could relocate elsewhere.
propositions.quote: The panel sees this simply as an indication that the claimant would be able to relocate elsewhere.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes the family still lives in Haryana; the claimant says they moved due to harassment, but the panel sees this as proof relocation is possible.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim.
propositions.quote: the panel rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim for the reasons given.
